learningObjective: Distinguish the abstractions and capabilities of graph-/operator-level IR (e.g., XLA HLO, ONNX) from loop/tensor-expression-level IR (e.g., TVM TensorIR, MLIR linalg/affine).

canonicalClaims.claim: Operator-level IRs abstract computations as coarse-grained ops with implicit iteration; loop-level IRs expose explicit loops and indexing, enabling per-loop transformations like tiling, unrolling, and vectorization.
conditions: The compiler stack maintains distinct dialects/levels for graph-level and loop-level reasoning.
nonImplications: Does not imply that a single IR cannot mix both abstractions (MLIR does).
Does not imply that loop-level IR is always better; op-level lets pattern rewrites remain compact.

canonicalClaims.claim: Operator-level IRs can annotate SSA values with static shape/dtype without exposing internal loop structure.
conditions: Shape/dtype are part of the value type.
nonImplications: Does not imply that shapes must be fully static; symbolic shape is also expressible in HLO/StableHLO and Relax.

misconceptions.claim: Operator-level IRs cannot express fusion; all fusion decisions require a loop-level IR.
misconceptions.whyWrong: XLA HLO fusion and TVM Relax operator fusion operate at the graph/operator level; loop-level IR is used for finer-grained loop-body fusion.

misconceptions.claim: Tiling and vectorization are graph-level transformations; they can be applied directly on operator-level IR.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Tile/vectorize/unroll act on explicit loops; without loops named in the IR, these transformations have no target.

misconceptions.claim: Operator-level IRs are shape-oblivious; only loop-level IRs know shapes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: HLO, StableHLO, ONNX, and TVM Relax all annotate values with shape and dtype.

misconceptions.claim: Loop-level IR is strictly more expressive than operator-level IR and should always be used first.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Operator-level IR is more compact for graph rewrites and dispatch; introducing loops too early inflates IR size and blocks graph-level pattern matches.

implementationFacts: XLA HLO / StableHLO: operator-level IR with static or symbolic shape annotations
MLIR linalg / affine: loop-level IR exposing iteration domains and access maps
TVM Relax → TensorIR: two-tier design mirroring operator-level to loop-level lowering
performanceScenarios: Graph-level fusion decisions typically happen at the operator level (which ops to group); loop-level fusion decisions happen when the fused pattern is lowered to explicit loops and iteration domains.
